checkpoint_scope: Fourteen passage-level analyses across two complete long-form technical texts. These analyses extract reasoning moves, evidence order, qualification discipline and reusable language behavior; they introduce no runtime facts.

long_form_texts.title: Water use in the United States energy system: A national assessment and unit process inventory of water consumption and withdrawals

passages.analytical_focus: Establish the gap before presenting scale.
passages.argument_move: The passage begins with incomplete national understanding, defines the base year and system coverage, and only then reports absolute and share-based results.
passages.evidence_structure: coverage -> definitions -> aggregate result -> dominant processes
passages.qualification_discipline: Results are tied to 2014, commercially traded primary energy and the stated accounting boundary.
passages.language_transfer: Lead a Water Read with what the evidence can measure, then state the bottleneck; do not open with an unbounded national number.
passages.anti_pattern: Headline scale without year, coverage and fate definition.

passages.analytical_focus: Explain why an apparently mature field still lacks a decision-ready total.
passages.argument_move: The authors connect outdated process factors, fragmented state reporting, inconsistent definitions and agency scope to the inability to co-manage water and energy.
passages.evidence_structure: institutional gap -> data-age problem -> classification mismatch -> decision consequence
passages.qualification_discipline: The critique distinguishes missing data from data that exist but cannot be combined safely.
passages.language_transfer: When disclosure is sparse, name the specific missing linkage rather than calling the entire domain opaque.
passages.anti_pattern: Treating fragmented evidence as no evidence or as a complete national inventory.

passages.location: pp. 7-10, system boundary and mass-transfer definitions
passages.analytical_focus: Make categories physical before comparing them.
passages.argument_move: The methods define withdrawal, consumption, source, quality, lifecycle stage and geographic boundary, then apply those definitions consistently to unusual flows such as produced water and inter-source transfers.
passages.qualification_discipline: Discharge and return flow are explicitly separated; embodied and foreign water are excluded.
passages.language_transfer: Use one plain definitional sentence when the Read turns on withdrawal versus consumption, then proceed to the comparison.
passages.anti_pattern: Using water use as a synonym for withdrawal, consumption, delivery and discharge.

passages.location: p. 8, evidence hierarchy and scaling proxies
passages.analytical_focus: Rank evidence and choose causal proxies.
passages.argument_move: Observed base-year data outrank recent compilations, operator communication, pre-operational estimates and physical calculations; scaling uses a process driver rather than a convenient output variable.
passages.evidence_structure: evidence rank -> missing-data fallback -> causal proxy -> validation
passages.qualification_discipline: A proxy is accepted only where its relationship to the water-using process is stated.
passages.language_transfer: Prefer direct facility evidence; if a proxy is unavoidable, state what physical relationship makes it relevant.
passages.anti_pattern: Scaling water by revenue, output or capacity merely because that denominator is available.

passages.location: pp. 13-16, withdrawal concentration and technology regimes
passages.analytical_focus: Locate the dominant mechanism rather than flattening a sector average.
passages.argument_move: The results separate groundwater production-stage consumption from surface-water conversion-stage withdrawals and identify a small once-through fleet as the dominant withdrawal mechanism.
passages.evidence_structure: fate split -> source split -> lifecycle split -> technology concentration
passages.qualification_discipline: Withdrawal dominance is not narrated as consumption dominance or local scarcity.
passages.language_transfer: Move from national context to the mechanism responsible for it, then stop before inferring facility availability.
passages.anti_pattern: Calling a withdrawal-intensive technology the largest consumer.

passages.analytical_focus: Prevent one environmental attribute from standing in for another.
passages.argument_move: The authors compare water outcomes within low-carbon resources and show that generation technology and cooling create large divergence despite a shared carbon label.
passages.evidence_structure: common category -> internal heterogeneity -> technology explanation -> transition implication
passages.qualification_discipline: The comparison preserves separate withdrawal and consumption intensities and excludes local stress claims.
passages.language_transfer: When linking Power to Water, describe the particular cooling and generation regime instead of equating low carbon with low water.
passages.anti_pattern: Using renewable, clean or low-carbon as a proxy for water performance.

passages.argument_move: The paper explains why single-year totals can outrank their allocated subtotals, how repeatedly transformed legacy factors lose provenance, and why ambiguous definitions create impossible national comparisons.
passages.evidence_structure: uncertainty source -> propagation mechanism -> reporting failure -> corrective rule
passages.qualification_discipline: Uncertainty is attached to specific allocations and data lineages rather than used as a blanket disclaimer.
passages.language_transfer: Qualify the exact inferential step that is weak; do not bury the whole Read under generalized uncertainty language.
passages.anti_pattern: Treating an old, repeatedly cited estimate as stronger because it appears in many secondary sources.

long_form_texts.title: The water use of data center workloads: A review and assessment of key determinants
long_form_texts.audited_version: complete 60-page accepted manuscript with supporting information

passages.location: pp. 2-5, metric critique and workload denominator
passages.analytical_focus: Match the denominator to the service being compared.
passages.argument_move: The authors show that site and source WUE per IT energy omit hardware performance, then introduce liters per benchmarked workload to compare unlike server efficiencies.
passages.evidence_structure: popular metric -> omitted variable -> comparison failure -> revised denominator
passages.qualification_discipline: The proposed workload metric is tied to a named benchmark and is not presented as universal computing output.
passages.language_transfer: State what a platform metric normalizes before using it to compare facilities or trends.
passages.anti_pattern: Calling lower WUE proof of lower water per digital service.

passages.analytical_focus: Expose the multiplicative pathways behind total water per workload.
passages.argument_move: Overall water is decomposed into direct facility water plus facility electricity multiplied by a grid water factor, with server efficiency and PUE feeding the electricity term.
passages.evidence_structure: system boundary -> equation -> component definitions -> determinant mapping
passages.qualification_discipline: Upstream, point-of-generation and on-site consumption remain inside named sub-boundaries.
passages.language_transfer: Build causal sentences around one conversion chain—workload, electricity, cooling or grid—not a list of disconnected water facts.
passages.anti_pattern: Adding site and grid water figures whose energy, time or geographic boundaries do not match.

passages.argument_move: Ten cooling configurations across nineteen climate zones show overlapping PUE and WUE outcomes, so no cooling label determines performance independently of climate and operating efficiency.
passages.evidence_structure: technology regimes -> climate regimes -> overlapping outcomes -> system-level implication
passages.qualification_discipline: Annual averages and modeled configuration ranges are not described as live facility measurements.
passages.language_transfer: Use cooling technology as a conditional mechanism: its effect depends on climate, controls and operating point.
passages.anti_pattern: Declaring liquid, evaporative, dry or free cooling categorically water-optimal.

passages.analytical_focus: Separate infrastructure efficiency from useful work.
passages.argument_move: The server model shows that efficiency quantile, utilization, refresh cycle and inactive share can produce the same electricity per workload through different combinations.
passages.evidence_structure: server state -> useful throughput -> energy per workload -> water implication
passages.qualification_discipline: The analysis notes diminishing inactive-server effects as newer servers lower idle power.
passages.language_transfer: When workload evidence is absent, do not infer service efficiency from facility PUE or total electricity alone.
passages.anti_pattern: Treating installed servers, nameplate IT capacity or electricity as delivered compute.

passages.location: pp. 17-23, grid water factor and source WUE
passages.argument_move: The analysis varies the grid water-consumption factor and shows that a low site WUE can coexist with high source WUE, while a water-using site can have a lower total under a low-water grid.
passages.evidence_structure: site metric -> grid factor -> combined metric -> reversal case
passages.qualification_discipline: Generation-weighted resource factors are identified as averages rather than dispatch-resolved attribution.
passages.language_transfer: Contrast on-site cooling and electricity-mediated water directly when the evidence supports both; never let one silently substitute for the other.
passages.anti_pattern: Ranking facilities on site WUE while omitting their electricity water boundary.

passages.location: pp. 23-26, Sobol sensitivity and no-silver-bullet result
passages.analytical_focus: Use sensitivity rankings as conditional decision support.
passages.argument_move: Variance decomposition ranks server efficiency, grid water factor and utilization while retaining cooling, climate and infrastructure as nontrivial interacting determinants; the policy section rejects a universal recipe.
passages.evidence_structure: global sensitivity -> ranked determinants -> constrained cases -> tailored action
passages.qualification_discipline: A variance contribution is not converted into a guaranteed savings percentage.
passages.language_transfer: Name the leading constraint for the observed case, then identify what would have to change; avoid generic solution lists.
passages.anti_pattern: Turning a modeled sensitivity rank into a universal causal effect size.

passages.analytical_focus: End with the exact boundary that controls interpretation.
passages.argument_move: The authors identify benchmark representativeness, omitted GPUs and networks, average grid factors, and consumption-only scope, then recommend separate withdrawal consideration and standardized footprint definitions.
passages.evidence_structure: model contribution -> omitted systems -> direction of bias -> next measurement need
passages.qualification_discipline: Each limitation is tied to how it could change the result rather than appended as ritual caveat.
passages.language_transfer: If a Water Read lacks facility evidence, conclude with the missing measurement that would change the inference—source, peak withdrawal, consumption, cooling or grid factor.
passages.anti_pattern: Ending with a broad call for more data without naming the decision-relevant missing field.

reusable_reasoning_moves: Define fate and boundary before reporting scale.
Move from aggregate context to the mechanism that creates it.
Rank evidence and preserve provenance through every proxy.
Match the denominator to useful service before comparing performance.
Treat cooling, climate, workload and grid water as interacting regimes.
Attach uncertainty to the weak inferential link, not the entire paragraph.
End on the measurement or conversion condition that would change the conclusion.
prose_controls: No more than two quantitative clauses in one sentence.
Use withdrawal, consumption, delivery, discharge and return flow only in their defined senses.
Avoid repeated thesis-restatement at paragraph endings.
Prefer mechanism verbs: withdraws, consumes, returns, supplies, constrains, converts, discloses.
Use exposure, estimate, scenario and observed only when the evidence class supports the term.
